ledger.claim: The route deviation is established on this trip's own trace. The GPS polyline measures 25.4 km against a booked optimal of 19.6 km, an excess of 5.8 km and 29.59%, which clears both POL-RD-01 gates: it exceeds 20% of optimal_distance_km and it exceeds 0.8 km in absolute terms. The governing figure is gps_trace.trace_distance_km; the trip_record's 25.4 km is only a rounded convenience copy of the same measurement.

This is an UPFRONT_QUOTE trip: fare_breakdown.fare_model is UPFRONT_QUOTE and quoted_fare_sgd is 24.50, so the distance and time charges were fixed at booking and POL-RD-02 does not run. The rider's remedy is therefore POL-RD-11(a): charged_total of 39.00 less quoted_fare_sgd of 24.50 less the pass-through and statutory lines properly chargeable under POL-RD-09 (0.00), which the ledger computes as a remedy of SGD 14.50, rounded up to the nearest SGD 0.05.

Neither charged ERP line is properly chargeable to this rider. The booked optimal route was PIE to Kallang then Nicoll Highway with optimal_route_erp_sgd of 0.00, while both charged gantries - ECP (Fort Rd towards City) and ECP (Rochor towards City), SGD 3.00 each - carry on_optimal_route false. They sit on a corridor the optimal route does not use, so the SGD 6.00 is not a pass-through the rider owes and is comprehended within the POL-RD-11(a) figure; it must not be counted a second time on top of that remedy.

The driver's explanation that 'PIE was crawling' rests on no artifact. EV-ADVIS-00501-01 is MISSING, carries no payload and has weight_multiplier 0.0 with issue code MISSING_ARTIFACT - I disclose the impairment. Under POL-RD-13 there is no traffic_advisory for this trip window, so POL-RD-03's comparison cannot be run, the clause is unavailable, and the assertion carries no weight under POL-RD-08. Because the driver names no advisory identifier, the missing artifact is a gap in the bundle and not a POL-RD-10(5) contradiction; the deviation stands at the measured figure.

The driver's fallback - that the rider agreed to the ECP detour - is equally unsupported. The trip's chat_log holds zero messages (message_count 0, empty array, first_message_at and last_message_at null), so there is no recorded rider instruction, no waypoint_hint and no road named. Under POL-RD-04 the instruction must come from the rider and be recorded in the chat_log, and the trace must corroborate it against the waypoint_hint field; with an empty log and a null hint the corroboration test is undecidable on the record, the clause is unavailable, and the defence is discarded under POL-RD-08 as an assertion citing no evidence.

Nothing about this trace triggers the integrity regime. It carries 163 fixes at a 10 second cadence over 100% coverage with no gaps and a max_gap_sec of 0.0, so none of POL-RD-07 limbs (a) to (c) fires: no gap over 90 seconds, no 500 m jump, no sustained interval above 30 seconds. The excess is therefore established on the trace itself without independent corroboration, and the escalation triggers in POL-RD-10(3) and POL-RD-10(5) are not engaged.

The rider's own record raises no additional hurdle. rider_profile.deviation_claims_60d is 0 and rider_profile.deviation_claims_60d_substantiated is 0, so the POL-RD-08 condition for demanding corroboration beyond the trace - four or more claims with one or fewer substantiated - is nowhere near met, and the rider's initial burden is discharged by the matched trip identifiers and the measured excess alone.

The outcome on the merits is a partial refund of SGD 14.50. The rider was quoted 24.50, agreed to pay 24.50, and was charged 39.00 once the driver left the optimal corridor for the ECP; under POL-RD-11 the 24.50 quoted fare stands and the 14.50 over-quote is returned, so the rider is left not carrying the disputed charge. I do not assert the full SGD 39.00 contested: the distance and time lines were fixed at booking and the remedy is the over-quote plus the improperly charged pass-through, not the whole fare.

This is an UPFRONT_QUOTE trip — fare_breakdown.fare_model is UPFRONT_QUOTE and quoted_fare_sgd is 24.50 — so POL-RD-11 governs and POL-RD-02 does not run. The distance and time lines were fixed at booking and, on this fare model, a detour costs the rider nothing on those lines; the 5.8 km excess therefore cannot be turned into a fare recomputation, and the recovery the claim implicitly seeks (the whole 39.00 back) is unavailable as a matter of the fare model.

On the ledger's own arithmetic the rider's recovery is confined to the POL-RD-11(a) correction: charged_total 39.00 less quoted_fare_sgd 24.50 less the properly chargeable pass-through and statutory lines of 0.00 = 14.50, the figure the ledger publishes as pol_rd_11_remedy. That 14.50 — not 39.00, and not the 16.50 implied by 'SGD 41 instead of 24' — is the ceiling on this dispute, and the rider's pleaded amount of 39.00 overstates it more than twofold.

The excess is 5.8 km on a 19.6 km booked optimal, i.e. 29.59%: it clears POL-RD-01's establishment tests (greater than 20% and greater than 0.8 km) but is well short of the 50% and 8.0 km materiality tests, so no MATERIAL deviation is recorded and POL-RD-06's material-deviation consequences cannot engage. In any event driver_profile.deviation_flags_90d is 0 against completed_trips_90d of 250, so no repeat pattern is established, no FULL_REFUND uplift is available, and no driver-conduct referral is warranted on this trip.

Both ECP charge lines are genuine crossings and not phantom lines: each gantry carries coordinates and the trace's nearest fix lies 0 m from it (fix indices 101 and 130), far inside the 250 m match radius POL-RD-09 sets. Nor is there an airport-surcharge defect — the trip originates at Changi T3 but the breakdown itemises airport_surcharge 0.00. There is accordingly no billing-integrity failure under POL-RD-09(4) and no referral on that basis.

If any pass-through correction is allowed it is already inside the 14.50: POL-RD-09(1) provides that off-route ERP is comprehended in the correction and must never be added on top of it. The 6.00 of ECP ERP (2 x 3.00) cannot be recovered twice, so the rider's total on this dispute remains 14.50 and no separate ERP sum is payable.

The driver's account that the rider agreed to the ECP routing is corroborated nowhere in the admitted evidence: EV-CHAT-00501 records zero messages for this trip. POL-RD-04 requires the rider's instruction to be recorded in the chat_log and corroborated by a waypoint_hint or a named road the trace follows; with no message at all the corroboration test cannot be run, the clause is unavailable, and — as POL-RD-04 itself directs — the case is decided on the remaining clauses. It follows equally that the rider's assertion that she was told nothing of extra charges rests on her own uncorroborated account, with no chat message to support it either.

The driver's traffic account is supported by no advisory record: EV-ADVIS-00501-01 is MISSING with weight_multiplier 0.0, so POL-RD-03 cannot be run, and under POL-RD-08 and POL-RD-13 an external-traffic assertion on this record neither reduces the measured excess nor supplies an amended optimal route. The absence of an advisory is a bundle gap that is itself citable, but it does not enlarge the claim against the driver either: the excess stands at the measured 5.8 km and the case is resolved on the trace and the ledger arithmetic.

ruling.explanation:
To both parties. The route is measured on this trip's own instruments and the fare is then settled under the rules for an upfront-quoted trip.

RIDER — the deviation is established. The GPS trace (EV-GPS-00501: 163 fixes at a 10-second cadence, 100% coverage, no gap, max gap 0.0 s) measures 25.4 km against the 19.6 km optimal recorded at booking on the trip record (EV-TRIP-00501): an excess of 5.8 km, or 29.59%. That passes both POL-RD-01 establishment tests (more than 0.8 km and more than 20%), so a deviation exists. It does not reach either materiality test (8.0 km or 50%), so it is not a MATERIAL deviation — no POL-RD-06 uplift and no conduct referral (the driver's deviation_flags_90d is 0 against 250 completed trips in any event). The trace is not impaired under POL-RD-07(a)-(c), so no independent corroboration is needed and POL-RD-10(3) does not fire.

The fare is upfront-quoted. EV-FARE-00501 shows fare_model UPFRONT_QUOTE, quoted_fare_sgd 24.50 and charged_total 39.00. Under POL-RD-11 the distance and time lines were fixed at booking, so POL-RD-02 is not run and the 5.8 km excess does not by itself produce a distance refund. Your remedy is POL-RD-11(a): charged_total 39.00 less the quoted fare 24.50 less the pass-through and statutory lines properly chargeable under POL-RD-09 (0.00) = SGD 14.50. The two ECP charges (3.00 + 3.00 = 6.00) are off the optimal corridor, whose own ERP is 0.00, so they are not properly chargeable and are already excluded inside the 14.50; they are not refunded a second time on top of it (POL-RD-09(1)). Your pleaded SGD 39.00 overstates the remedy; the amount returned is SGD 14.50, rounded up to the nearest 5 cents.

DRIVER — your traffic explanation ('PIE was crawling') is unsupported. No traffic advisory covers this trip: EV-ADVIS-00501-01 is MISSING, weight_multiplier 0.0, issue code MISSING_ARTIFACT; its absence is itself citable but it carries no fact, so POL-RD-03 cannot be run and the assertion carries no weight under POL-RD-08 and POL-RD-13. Because no advisory identifier was named, this is a gap in the bundle and not a POL-RD-10(5) escalation, and the missing artifact does not cap confidence. Your fallback that the rider agreed to the ECP routing also fails: EV-CHAT-00501 holds zero messages, so there is no recorded rider instruction, no waypoint_hint and no named road, and POL-RD-04's corroboration test is undecidable on the record — the clause is unavailable and the defence is discarded under POL-RD-08.

The two ERP lines are genuine crossings (the trace's nearest fix lies 0 m from each gantry, inside the 250 m radius) and the airport surcharge of 0.00 is not a defect, so there is no billing-integrity failure under POL-RD-09(4) and no referral on that ground. No profile field has been used to establish anything about this trip (POL-GEN-01). Confidence is 0.90: the deciding facts — the measured excess and the fare arithmetic — are carried by the GPS trace, the trip record and the fare breakdown, each at weight 1.0, so the cap is 1.0, above the 0.70 floor.

Outcome: PARTIAL_REFUND of SGD 14.50 to the rider; the driver receives no compensation (the billed distance equals the traced distance, so POL-RD-04's compensation limb has no shortfall to work on).

The judge was asked 4 times on the same inputs and every draft agreed on this ruling, so it is carried unanimously (vote agreement 1.00).
